description.narrative: The program seeks to help the state government of Mizoram (SGM) to create fiscal space by (i) enhancing tax and nontax revenue measures and rationalizing expenditures; (ii) bringing about service improvements in two key sectors (health and education) in a cost-effective manner; (iii) ensuring better debt management; (iv) reforming the state pension system; and (v) restructuring public sector enterprises, including through closure, as needed.

description.narrative: Creation of greater fiscal space in, and financial flexibility of, the budget of the state government of Mizoram

At least zero revenue deficit during the entire program period or in line with any other numerical target specified by the Thirteenth Finance Commission. (2007/08 baseline: $27 million revenue surplus) Progress/Status: The revenue surplus stood at Rs166.3 million—0.3% of the gross state domestic product (GSDP)—in FY2010 (revised estimate) Data Source: Central statistical organization reports
RBI reports on state finances Actual value:

Deficits are within prescribed limits of the FRBM Act without resorting to capital expenditure reductions, with a fiscal deficit of 3% or in line with any other numerical target specified by the Thirteenth Finance Commission. (2008 baseline: 3.8%) Progress/Status: The fiscal deficit continues to be high at almost 11% of GSDP in FY2010. Data Source: Finance accounts and budget document of SGM
FRBM compliance reports Actual value:

Twenty percent increase in own revenue, with 2007/08 as the baseline. (2007/08 baseline: $43 million) Data Source: Special coordinated joint monitoring by Government and ADB
Loan review missions Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. Tax and nontax revenue reforms successfully implemented Indicator: At least the top three most serious risk-based cases scrutinized and reassessed. (2008 baseline: none reassessed) Actual value:

Output: 2. Government debts are effectively restructured and managed Indicator: All contingent liabilities guaranteed by the guarantee redemption fund. (2008 baseline: 0%, policy decision already taken on fund establishment) Progress/Status: A risk assessment report was prepared detailing probabilities of default of various loans guaranteed by the state. The guarantee redemption fund (GRF) has been augmented by Rs.10 million and documented in the budget for FY2011. Data Source: Reports of consultants and vendors Actual value:

Output: 2. Government debts are effectively restructured and managed Indicator: All staff responsible for debt management skilled in use of debt database management. (2008 baseline: none, capacity building plan being developed) Data Source: RBI reports Actual value:

Output: 2. Government debts are effectively restructured and managed Indicator: Documentation of all incurred debts and contingent liabilities in a debt database. (2008 baseline: 0% in database, relevant software identified) Data Source: Loan review missions Actual value:

Output: 3. The management of public expenditure is rationalized Indicator: All public investment decisions of the state government are vetted by the FMC. (2008 baseline: 0%, FMC established early 2009) Data Source: Finance Department notifications and reports
Budget statements Actual value:

Output: 3. The management of public expenditure is rationalized Indicator: Well-documented MTEFs in place for the departments of health and family welfare and of school education based on relevant long-term sector strategy and road map. (2008 baseline: no MTEF in place) Progress/Status: The Department of Health and Family Welfare and the Department of School Education have prepared rolling MTEFs for their departments based on the projected resources available and sectoral goals/targets. Both MTEFs have been prepared and extensive training of staff has been provided. The real benefits from these initiatives will emerge when the two departments need to prepare their budgets for 2012-2013 based on the MTEFs (third-tranche policy action). Data Source: Department reports and statements
Loan review missions Actual value:

Output: 4. Services in the health and education sectors are more accessible and improved Indicator: SGM able to provide VRS to all eligible and interested teachers. (2008 baseline: none, VRS yet to be finalized) Data Source: Department reports and statements, including from Mizoram Health Care Society Actual value:

Output: 5. The government pension scheme is reformed and made more financially sustainable Indicator: All new recruits in state government are covered by the defined contributory pension scheme. (2008 baseline: none, the scheme is not yet in place) Progress/Status: As envisaged under the second tranche of the program, the state introduced, through notification on 17 June 2010, a defined-contribution pension scheme for state government employees recruited on or after 1 September 2010. Data Source: Finance Department notifications and reports
Budget statements Actual value:
Output: 6. Loss-making PSEs are restructured or closed Indicator: All restructured PSEs have good practice corporate governance standards in place. (2008 baseline: none) Actual value:

Output: 6. Loss-making PSEs are restructured or closed Indicator: At least one PSE contributes dividends to the state treasury by 3 years of program-end. (2008 baseline: none) Data Source: Reports from the PSEs Actual value:

Output: 6. Loss-making PSEs are restructured or closed Indicator: At least one PSE, from the set of PSEs selected for closure, is closed. (2008 baseline: no such set determined yet) Data Source: Notification and annual reports by the Finance Department Actual value:

Output: 1. Tax and nontax revenue reforms successfully implemented Indicator: User charges for water usage covers at least 50% of O&M costs. (2008 baseline: 16%) Progress/Status: The notification to revise the water charges for commercial and noncommercial users was issued on 10 June 2011. The implementation report on the methodology of quality- and cost-based user charge recovery has been prepared and submitted to the Department of Finance. Data Source: RBI reports on state finances Actual value:

Output: 3. The management of public expenditure is rationalized Indicator: No more than 5% variance in the annual budgets of the departments of health and family welfare and of school education from their respective MTEFs. (2006/07-2007/08 estimated baseline: 12% for health and 16% for education) Data Source: Independent evaluations
Reports from vendors Actual value:

Output: 4. Services in the health and education sectors are more accessible and improved Indicator: At least 30% of households headed by women and 60% of families living below the poverty line covered under the MHC Scheme. (2008 baseline: 17.3% for households headed by women and 0.5% for families living below the poverty line) Data Source: Finance Department notifications and reports
Budget statements Actual value:

Output: 1. Tax and nontax revenue reforms successfully implemented Indicator: Tax arrears reduced by 50%. (2008 baseline: $25 million) Progress/Status: The state of Mizoram has prepared and approved detailed plans for collection of tax arrears. The action plan for the Department of Taxation includes (i) updating of the existing data; (ii) information collection; (iii) public awareness campaigns; (iv) penalty on defaults; and (v) a strategic plan to avoid arrear accumulation (e.g., denial of statutory forms to registered taxpayers (dealers) so as to restrict the entry of their goods within the state unless tax arrears are cleared). The Deputy Commissioner (Investigation) at the Commissionerate Office is entrusted with the responsibility of supervising the process of collecting arrears. For the zones, the Assistant Commissioner of Taxes and the Superintendent of Taxes will be the main supervising officers. A system of monthly reports prepared by the zonal offices on the up-to-date status of arrear collection has also been introduced. Data Source: Government notifications, auction award letters, and circulars Actual value:
Output: 6. Loss-making PSEs are restructured or closed Indicator: PSE employment levels remain at least constant to the 2008 baseline. (2008 baseline: 266 employees) Actual value:
Output: 2. Government debts are effectively restructured and managed Indicator: No increase in contingent liabilities to GSDP ratio during program period. (2008 baseline: 4%) Actual value:

Output: 1. Tax and nontax revenue reforms successfully implemented Indicator: Twenty percent improvement in own source revenue collection. (2007/08 baseline: $43 million) Data Source: Department reports Actual value:

Output: 1. Tax and nontax revenue reforms successfully implemented Indicator: Maximum professional tax (as per Constitution of India) imposed on selected nonsalaried professional groups. (2008 baseline: only 50% of ceiling imposed) Progress/Status: The state has issued and notified an increase in the professional tax rates within the ceiling fixed by the Constitution of India. The notification was issued on 23 May 2011. Over and above upward revisions in the tax rates across various income classes and professions, the exemption limit was reduced from Rs10,000 to Rs5,000. 14. The reforms pertaining to nontax revenue primarily focused on more efficient collection of user charges based on a feasible plan for cost recovery and revision of the water charges. Data Source: Budget speeches of finance minister Actual value:

Output: 1. Tax and nontax revenue reforms successfully implemented Indicator: At least 20% increase in revenues from stamp duties and registration fees. (2008 baseline: $0.05 million) Progress/Status: The state issued notification on 22 February 2011 to impose stamp duty on all bills concerning payments to private parties. Data Source: Status reports submitted by the Department of Finance Actual value:

Output: 2. Government debts are effectively restructured and managed Indicator: Premature retirement of at least 80% of high-cost debt (with interest rate >9%). (2008 baseline: $58 million high-cost debt, excluding Government loans) Progress/Status: The state used $19 million equivalent out of the first-tranche funds for early repayment of high-cost debt Data Source: DOF notifications and reports Actual value:
Output: 6. Loss-making PSEs are restructured or closed Indicator: Government outlays on PSEs remain constant to the 2006/07 baseline. (2006/07 baseline: $0.9 million) Actual value:
7. Program supervision and management.

Output: 10. Preparation of MTEFs (LN 2537) Indicator: The loan will provide support to the departments of health and family welfare, of school education, and of finance to prepare and implement MTEFs; this will include expert advice and training.

Output: 11. Treasury Automation (LN 2537) Indicator: Support to the Department of Finance to automate the nine treasuries in the state will begin with a pilot of the largest treasury (South Aizawl) and, based on its success, the other eight will be computerized during the program period. The TA will provide equipment and technology, and training support for management of the new systems Progress/Status: Pilot computerization of the South Aizawl Treasury has been completed, Training and hands-on support has been provided by INGAF and NIC, COMPACT (software) readiness assessment was conducted by NIC and INGAF on 20-22 June 2011. Evaluation report and roadmap for computerization of other eight treasuries have been prepared.

Output: 12. Debt Management (LN 2537) Indicator: The loan will provide support to enhance capacity in various areas of debt management, including coordinating public debt information, analyzing total public debt, and developing debt policies and strategies. Progress/Status: A separate debt management unit has been established in the Department of Finance, A debt management manual has been prepared, Training of staff in debt management software and related issues will start in September 2011.

Output: 13. Support to Program Management (LN 2537) Indicator: The loan will provide support to program management and coordination. Support to program management will include efforts to: (i) build the capacity of relevant sector ministries (i.e., education and health) to collect gender-disaggregated information on a systematic basis, and (ii) ensure that gender considerations are strongly taken into account in the implementation of the program, particularly the subcomponent of the program that focuses on service Progress/Status: FMU staff and other staff from the PIUs attended ADB's capacity building training in Delhi and Guwahati (Assam), Basic requirements of office equipments have been procured by FMU, Plans for gender mapping in health and education sectors are being prepared.

Output: 4. Services in the health and education sectors are more accessible and improved Indicator: All new recruitment of teachers from FY2010 is by documented merit criteria, and in consonance with all policies for equal employment. (2008 baseline: merit criteria finalized) Data Source: Reports from vendors

Output: 4. Services in the health and education sectors are more accessible and improved Indicator: At least 90% of teachers that opt for VRS are replaced by suitably qualified teachers. (2008 baseline: VRS not in place) Progress/Status: In the first phase so far, 193 underqualified primary school teachers have taken voluntary retirement. The selection of new, qualified teachers is underway. Underqualified middle school teachers are targeted in the second phase. Data Source: Loan review missions
Independent surveys and evaluations

Output: 5. The government pension scheme is reformed and made more financially sustainable Indicator: Fully functional pension database of existing pension scheme. (2008 baseline: no such database in place) Data Source: Department reports and statements
Loan review missions Baseline year: 2008 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2008 Baseline value: N Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 8. Revenue Administration (LN 2537) Indicator: The loan will support computerization of land revenue processes and offices, as well as capacity building in the area of revenue administration. The main areas of focus are: (i) a functional requirement study based on the tax reform road map prepared by SGM, (ii) preparation of bidding documents for procurement of services of vendors for developing the tax information management system, (iii) bid process management, (iv) strengthening of audit processes, (v) program management support for implementation of the information system, and (vi) training for revenue department officials. Progress/Status: Capacity building training is ongoing for the various components such as land record management. Ten rounds of capacity building training have already been completed. Bidding documents for procurement of items for MIS will be finalized once the selection of the firm for MIS is completed (expected by Nov 2011).

Output: 9. Project Appraisal and Monitoring (LN 2537) Indicator: The loan will provide: (i) support to establish the finance commission and project monitoring cell in the Department of Finance to ensure rigorous appraisal of government projects, and (ii) expert advice to the cell on relevant processes. Progress/Status: Project appraisal manual completed and notified. Workshop has been held in Aizawl.
